subject: POC cadence, acceptance criteria, owners and kickoff availability
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Lina Torres <lina.torres@aureus.health>, Michael Chen <michael.chen@aureus.health>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 29 May 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: POC cadence, acceptance criteria, owners and kickoff availability

Hi Lina / Michael — thanks again for a productive discovery earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can lock the POC cadence and owners. If I missed anything, please flag it inline.

Summary of what Aureus needs to validate (candidate acceptance criteria)
- Latency: 95th percentile inference latency under 300ms for clinical triage queries (avg query length ~120 tokens)
- Throughput: sustainable 100 requests/min with burst up to 250/min during simulated peak
- Quality: >92% top-1 accuracy on the 150-case clinician prompt set you shared (we'll run blind eval)
- Security: no PHI retention beyond session; proof of SOC2 controls or SOC2-equivalent calendar for audit

Proposed POC plan (high level)
- Kickoff: week of June 7 (we suggested Tue/Wed Jun 8–9; open to other days)
- Duration: 3 weeks active run (config, baseline, 2-week evaluation window) + 1 week readout
- Cadence: 30-minute weekly engineering check-ins (Mon 10am PT) + 1 executive sync at readout
- Owners: Marissa (AE) — overall timeline/roadmap; Sean (CS) — technical runbook and test harness; Michael (Aureus) — clinical test owner; Lina (Aureus) — procurement/security gate

Immediate asks for Aureus to unblock kickoff
1) Confirm kickoff date (we tentatively hold Jun 8).
2) Share final 150-case test set by Jun 4 (anonymized CSV preferred).
3) Confirm who will run account-level load tests and whether we can use a separate test org/api key.
4) Any procurement requirements or PO timing we should know about?

Attachments: I attached a one-page runbook summary and milestone matrix for quick reference (redwood-poc-runbook-v1.md, poc-milestone-matrix.xlsx).

If that looks good I will send a short mutual action plan link and calendar invites for the proposed cadence.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0193

From: Lina Torres <lina.torres@aureus.health>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Michael Chen <michael.chen@aureus.health>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC cadence, acceptance criteria, owners and kickoff availability

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side and a small ask before we confirm Jun 8: 

Acceptance criteria tweaks
- Latency: can we make the 95th percentile target 350ms for burst windows? Our infra has variable routing; we can accept 350ms if steady-state stays under 300ms.
- Quality: please confirm how you will score 'top-1 accuracy' (exact match vs human adjudication). We prefer a blinded adjudication step for borderline cases.

Security/compliance
- Procurement needs a short SOC2 evidence bundle (controls summary + latest report stub). Can you attach a SOC2 summary we can share with procurement?
- We will require a data handling statement for the trial specifying no PHI persistence, token-level logging disabled by default, and a contact for incident response.

Logistics
- Jun 8 works for the clinical team but our infra lead Michael Chen asked whether Redwood can provide a temporary test API key scoped to the POC org and a short runbook for load tests.
- Procurement needs to see estimated POC consumption costs to approve the PO — can you provide a ballpark?

Attached: SOC2_summary_AureusRequest.pdf (redacted). Michael — can you confirm which weekday works best for the 30-min checkpoints? We prefer morning PT.

Thanks,
Lina Torres
Head of Clinical Programs | Aureus Health
lina.torres@aureus.health

Subject: RE: POC cadence, acceptance criteria, owners and kickoff availability

Thanks Marissa / Lina — jumping in with the technical plan and a couple of concrete asks so we can land the test harness by kickoff. I attached the full runbook but the key points below: 

Technical POC runbook (high level)- Environment: we'll provision a dedicated POC model instance in Redwood's sandbox org; you will get a scoped API key which can be revoked at any time.
- Test harness: we will ship a small harness that can run the 150-case set against multiple throughput/load profiles (baseline, 100rpm sustained, 250rpm burst). We recommend running the baseline first, then the 2 throughput profiles on separate days.
- Data handling: logs will be tokenized and only error traces (no full prompts) will be stored for debugging; we will disable any persistent session storage by default for the trial.
- Scoring: we will produce raw predictions plus a CSV with confidences; Aureus will perform blinded adjudication and return labels for final scoring. We can optionally run a small adjudication UI if helpful.

Concrete asks for Aureus before Jun 8 kickoff
1) Final CSV test set (anonymized) by EOD Jun 4.
2) Email the person who will run the harness from your side and confirm SSH access to test infra if you plan to run local load tests.
3) Procurement: an approximate POC cost estimate — we suggest sending a short cost bucket: compute + token units. Marissa, I put a placeholder in the runbook.

I'll hold the shared runbook in Drive and update it after we get the test set. Looking forward to the kickoff — I'll reserve time Jun 8 10:00am PT for the first engineering sync unless I hear otherwise.

Attachments: redwood-poc-runbook-v1.md (contains milestone matrix and test commands).

—Sean
